title: CSPO: Constraint-Sensitive Policy Optimization for Safe Reinforcement Learning
claim: Standard primal-dual updates overshoot and oscillate near steep constraint boundaries; scaling the correction by constraint sensitivity gives stable, direct recovery.
layout: single panel, top-to-bottom trajectories over contour plot, callout annotation and legend
description: A single 2-D toy optimization landscape. Dashed colored ellipses show the objective level sets. Dotted colored curves show the constraint level sets. A thick dark purple curve marks the constraint boundary g(θ)=0, and a light teal shading marks the infeasible region on the right. A blue dot labeled π0 sits in the infeasible region near the top. A teal dot labeled π_safe* sits on the boundary near the bottom. A blue dashed path (Primal-dual) wiggles and loops across the boundary, overshooting on the way down. An orange solid path (CSPO) goes smoothly and almost directly from π0 to the safe point. A callout at the top reads 'Steep constraint surface (large ||∇g(θ)||)' with an arrow pointing to the crowded dotted contours. A legend at bottom left names the two methods. The eye goes first to the two contrasting trajectories.
caption: Geometric intuition for CSPO on a toy constrained optimization problem. Dashed curves denote objective level sets f(θ), dotted curves denote constraint level sets g(θ), the purple curve is the boundary g(θ) = 0, and the shaded region is infeasible. Starting from an infeasible iterate π0, standard Lagrangian updates may overshoot and oscillate in highly sensitive regions, whereas CSPO scales the constraint correction by |∇g(θ)|, enabling stable recovery to feasibility with reduced reward degradation.
abstract: Safe reinforcement learning (Safe RL) aims to maximize expected return while satisfying safety constraints, typically modeled as Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs). While primal-dual methods scale well to deep RL, they often suffer from delayed constraint correction, leading to oscillatory behavior and prolonged safety violations. In this paper, we propose Constraint-Sensitive Policy Optimization (CSPO), a first-order primal-dual method that incorporates local constraint sensitivity into policy updates. CSPO augments the primal objective with a constraint-sensitive correction derived from the shortest signed distance to the safety boundary, enabling smarter recovery steps back to safety, compensating for delayed Lagrange multiplier updates, reducing oscillations near the boundary, and preserving the KKT solutions of the original constrained problem. Experiments on navigation and locomotion benchmarks demonstrate that CSPO achieves faster safety recovery and high reward preservation, resulting in higher constrained returns compared to state-of-the-art primal-dual and penalty-based methods
